articles.title: Email attachments, shared folders or forms: which should your business use?
articles.article_format: Commercial comparison with an intake-channel decision matrix
articles.target_client_type: Operationally complex UK SMEs receiving repeated customer, supplier or internal data and documents through email, shared folders or forms
articles.industry_or_operating_context: Broader UK SME operations across ecommerce, wholesale, distribution, service, professional-services, finance and administration teams

rolling_12_portfolio_mix_after_publicati.note: The rolling 12 remains core-market heavy because of the initial publication history. This broader-SME article continues the planned shift towards a 4 core / 8 broader balance.

articles.primary_buyer_problem: Incoming data and documents arrive through the wrong channel, creating missing fields, duplicate versions, chasing and re-keying before work can begin.
articles.primary_search_intent: Compare email attachments, shared folders and structured forms for repeated business data and document intake.
articles.primary_query: email attachments shared folders or forms
related_query_family: shared folder vs email for documents
how to collect customer data without email
articles.trend_or_durable_demand: Durable operational demand. UK SMEs continue to receive repeated data and documents through mixed channels, creating a recurring decision about structure, access, retention and system entry.
articles.evidence_source_and_date: Durable-demand classification based on the site's current process clusters and the recurring operational need evidenced by existing intake, invoice, spreadsheet and system hand-off workflows; assessed 31 July 2026.
articles.what_changed_or_matters: No current platform development was required. The article addresses a durable commercial decision that directly affects data quality, repair work and the cost of later automation.
articles.existing_article_gap: The site covered invoice controls, spreadsheet operating rules and system hand-offs, but did not compare the entry channels used before data reaches those workflows.
articles.henry_distinct_contribution: A process-design and control view: select the intake channel by data structure, access, retention and downstream use rather than defaulting to email or forcing every case into a form.

overlaps_considered: Your spreadsheet is not the problem. The missing operating rules are.

rolling_12_article_audit.why_distinct: This article decides how work should enter a process. It does not focus on spreadsheet governance, invoice approval, architecture selection or wholesale order entry. Its central mechanism is an intake-channel comparison covering mailbox parsers, folder watchers and form validation.

articles.original_editorial_asset: A five-factor intake-channel decision matrix comparing email attachments, shared folders and structured forms by use case, risk, automation method, human review and selection rule.
articles.first_hand_contribution_or_limits: Uses Henry Oliver's operating, consulting, data and control perspective. It does not claim first-hand experience inside unrelated client industries and does not use an invented case study.
articles.proof_points_used_recently: The 200,000-SKU and eight-hours-to-two-minutes proof points were not reused.
